arxiv-2102-03389.title: Online Statistical Inference for Stochastic Optimization via Kiefer-Wolfowitz Methods
arxiv-2102-03389.creator: Xi Chen Zehua Lai He Li Yichen Zhang
arxiv-2102-03389.description: Abstract This paper investigates the problem of online statistical inference of model parameters in stochastic optimization problems via the Kiefer-Wolfowitz algorithm with random search directions. We first present the asymptotic distribution for the Polyak-Ruppert-averaging type Kiefer-Wolfowitz (AKW) estimators, whose asymptotic covariance matrices depend on the distribution of search directions and the function-value query complexity.

arxiv-2103-07289.title: Searching by Generating: Flexible and Efficient One-Shot NAS with Architecture Generator
arxiv-2103-07289.creator: Sian-Yao Huang and Wei-Ta Chu National Cheng Kung University, Tainan, Taiwan {P76084245,wtchu}@gs.ncku.edu.tw
arxiv-2103-07289.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sian-Yao Huang and Wei-Ta Chu National Cheng Kung University, Tainan, Taiwan {P76084245,wtchu}@gs.ncku.edu.tw. In one-shot NAS, sub-networks need to be searched from the supernet to meet different hardware constraints. However, the search cost is high and N N times of searches are needed for N N different constraints. In this work, we propose a novel search strategy called architecture generator to search sub-networks by generating them, so that the search process can be much more efficient and flexible.

arxiv-2204-14256.title: Handling and Presenting Harmful Text in NLP Research
arxiv-2204-14256.creator: Hannah Rose Kirk, Abeba Birhane, Bertie Vidgen, Leon Derczynski
arxiv-2204-14256.description: Abstract Text data can pose a risk of harm. However, the risks are not fully understood, and how to handle, present, and discuss harmful text in a safe way remains an unresolved issue in the NLP community. We provide an analytical framework categorising harms on three axes: (1) the harm type (e.g.

arxiv-2302-12662.title: FedDBL: Communication and Data Efficient Federated Deep-Broad Learning for Histopathological Tissue Classification
arxiv-2302-12662.creator: Tianpeng Deng, Yanqi Huang, Zhenwei Shi, Jiatai Lin, Qi Dou, Zaiyi Liu, Xiao-jing Guo, C. L. Philip Chen, Chu Han
arxiv-2302-12662.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tianpeng Deng, Yanqi Huang, Zhenwei Shi, Jiatai Lin, Qi Dou, Zaiyi Liu, Xiao-jing Guo, C. L. Philip Chen, Chu Han. Histopathological tissue classification is a fundamental task in computational pathology. Deep learning-based models have achieved superior performance but centralized training with data centralization suffers from the privacy leakage problem.

arxiv-2303-16195.title: When to be critical? Performance and evolvability in different regimes of neural Ising agents.
arxiv-2303-16195.creator: Sina Khajehabdollahi ⋆ ( @sinak12345 ), Jan Prosi ⋆ ( @Jan_psi ), Emmanouil Giannakakis ( @m_giannakakis ), Georg Martius ( @GMartius ), Anna Levina ( @SelfOrgAnna )
arxiv-2303-16195.description: Abstract It has long been hypothesized that operating close to the critical state is beneficial for natural, artificial and their evolutionary systems. We put this hypothesis to test in a system of evolving foraging agents controlled by neural networks that can adapt agents’ dynamical regime throughout evolution. Surprisingly, we find that all populations that discover solutions, evolve to be subcritical.

arxiv-2307-04206.title: Multi-mission view of low-luminosity ‘obscured’ phase of GRS 1915+105 2022 Multi-mission view of low-luminosity ‘obscured’ phase of GRS 1915+105 – References
arxiv-2307-04206.creator: Athulya M. P, Anuj Nandi
arxiv-2307-04206.description: Abstract GRS 1915+105 is observed in an ‘obscured’ phase since May 2019, exhibiting steady and low X-ray luminosities, while being intervened by sporadic re-brightenings. In this work, we perform a comprehensive and wide-band analysis of the spectral and timing properties of the source during the period 2019–2021 using AstroSat ( SXT : 0.5–8 keV; LAXPC : 3–60 keV), NICER (0.

arxiv-2309-03106.description: Abstract In this paper, we develop the numerical inverse scattering transform (NIST) for solving the derivative nonlinear Schr ​ o ¨ ​ dinger \rm Schr\ddot{o}dinger (DNLS) equation. The key technique involves formulating a Riemann-Hilbert problem (RHP) that is associated with the initial value problem and solving it numerically. Before solving the RHP, two essential operations need to be carried out.

arxiv-2403-16673.title: Quasi-randomization tests for network interference
arxiv-2403-16673.creator: Supriya Tiwari and Pallavi Basu
arxiv-2403-16673.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Supriya Tiwari and Pallavi Basu. Network interference amounts to the treatment status of one unit affecting the potential outcome of other units in the population. Testing for spillover effects in this setting makes the null hypothesis non-sharp. An interesting approach to tackling the non-sharp nature of the null hypothesis in this setup is constructing conditional randomization tests such that the null is sharp on the restricted population.

arxiv-2406-04653.title: Dynamical mixture modeling with fast, automatic determination of Markov chains
arxiv-2406-04653.creator: Christopher E. Miles, Robert J. Webber
arxiv-2406-04653.description: Abstract Markov state modeling has gained popularity in various scientific fields due to its ability to reduce complex time series data into transitions between a few states. Yet, current frameworks are limited by assuming a single Markov chain describes the data, and they suffer an inability to discern heterogeneities.

arxiv-2407-04094.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by L. Ighina, A. Caccianiga, A. Moretti, J. W. Broderick, J. K. Leung, A. R. López-Sánchez, F. Rigamonti, N. Seymour, T. An, S. arxiv-2502-20405.title: Pause-Tuning for Long-Context Comprehension: A Lightweight Approach to LLM Attention Recalibration
arxiv-2502-20405.creator: James Begin Namit Agrawal Eshan Singh Yicheng Fu Sean O’Brien Vasu Sharma Kevin Zhu
arxiv-2502-20405.description: Abstract LLMs have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in understanding tasks but continue to struggle with long-context comprehension, particularly with content located in the middle of extensive inputs. This limitation, known as the Lost-in-the-Middle (LITM) problem, hinders models from fully processing and utilizing information across lengthy contexts.

arxiv-2509-10089.title: KAN-SR: A Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Guided Symbolic Regression Framework
arxiv-2509-10089.creator: Marco A. Bühler, Gonzalo Guillén-Gosálbez
arxiv-2509-10089.description: Abstract We introduce a novel symbolic regression framework, namely KAN-SR, built on Kolmogorov Arnold Networks (KANs) which follows a divide-and-conquer approach. Symbolic regression searches for mathematical equations that best fit a given dataset and is commonly solved with genetic programming approaches.

arxiv-2509-15334.title: VVV-WIT-13: an eruptive young star with cool molecular features
arxiv-2509-15334.creator: Zhen Guo ,, P. Lucas, S. N. Yurchenko, T. Kaminski, M. Montesinos, S. Nayakshin, V. Elbakyan, J. Osses, A. Caratti o Garatti, H. Zhao, R. Kurtev, J. Borissova, C. Morris, D. Minniti, J. Alonso-García, V. Fermiano, R. K. Saito, N. Miller, G. Zsidi, H. D. S. Muthu, C. Briceño, C. Contreras Peña, A. E.
arxiv-2509-15334.description: Abstract Context. Outburst phenomena are observed at different stages of stellar evolution, due to the enhancement of mass accretion rate on protostars or even stellar merger events. In the case of a Young Stellar Object (YSO), the episodic mass accretion event plays an important role in the pre-main-sequence stellar mass assembly.

arxiv-2511-09123.title: Private Remote Phase Estimation over a Lossy Quantum Channel
arxiv-2511-09123.creator: Farzad Kianvash, Marco Barbieri, Matteo Rosati
arxiv-2511-09123.description: Abstract Private remote quantum sensing (PRQS) aims at estimating a parameter at a distant location by transmitting quantum states on an insecure quantum channel, limiting information leakage and disruption of the estimation itself from an adversary. Previous results highlighted that one can bound the estimation performance in terms of the observed noise.

arxiv-2601-00634.title: THERMODYNAMIC FORMALISM OF STOCHASTIC EQUILIBRIUM ECONOMICS
arxiv-2601-00634.creator: Esa Nummelin, Elja Arjas
arxiv-2601-00634.description: Abstract In economics, construction of perfect models in a way that would be comparable to the standards customary in physical sciences is generally not feasible. In particular, the observed value for an economic equilibrium may deviate significantly from its model-based a priori expected value.

pmc-10709464.title: Impact of gamification on green consumption behavior integrating technological awareness, motivation, enjoyment and virtual CSR
pmc-10709464.creator: Muhammad Farrukh Shahzad, Shuo Xu, Obaid ul Rehman, Iqra Javed
pmc-10709464.description: Gamification entails integrating game design elements, including rewards, points, competition, and interactive challenges, into non-game contexts to engage and motivate individuals. In the context of green consumption, gamification can encourage individuals to acquire more sustainable consumption behaviors. The proposed study aims to examine the influence of gamification on green consumption behavior among Chinese university students.

pmc-10735247.title: Comprehensive Comparison of AAV Purification Methods: Iodixanol Gradient Centrifugation vs. Immuno-Affinity Chromatography
pmc-10735247.creator: Anh K. Lam, Patrick L. Mulcrone, Dylan Frabutt, Junping Zhang, Matthew Chrzanowski, Sreevani Arisa, Maite Munoz, Xin Li, Moanaro Biswas, David Markusic, Roland W. Herzog, Weidong Xiao
pmc-10735247.description: Recombinant adeno-associated viruses (AAVs) have emerged as a widely used gene delivery platform for both basic research and human gene therapy. To ensure and improve the safety profile of AAV vectors, substantial efforts have been dedicated to the vector production process development using suspension HEK293 cells.

pmc-10750633.title: Evaluation of Mechanical Stress Distribution Across the Calcaneus following Calcaneal Autograft: A Finite Element Analysis
pmc-10750633.creator: Mohammad T. Azam, Nicholas Parody, Thelma R. Jimenez Mosquea, James J. Butler, Hugo A. Ubillus, John G. Kennedy, Raymond J. Walls
pmc-10750633.description: Category:OtherIntroduction/Purpose:The purpose of this study was to utilize finite element analysis to evaluate progressive bone removal from the calcaneus at various angles and its effect on the mechanical stress distribution at the calcaneus, and potential increase in fracture risk.Methods:A calcaneus CT scan was imported into Autodesk Fusion360 (Autodesk, v.2.0.14569).

pmc-11414031.title: High-frequency magnetic paired associated stimulation promotes motor function recovery in ischemic stroke patients: a study protocol for single-center, sham stimulation randomized controlled trials (H2MPAS)
pmc-11414031.creator: Guangyue Zhu, Shuping Wang, Guodong Zhang, Yu Zhang, Zhexue Huang, Xiaoshun Tan, Yuhui Chen, Hui Sun, Dongsheng Xu
pmc-11414031.description: BackgroundNumerous studies have validated the clinical effectiveness of electromagnetic pairing-associated stimulation. Building upon this foundation, we have developed a novel approach involving high-frequency magnetic paired-associated stimulation, aiming to enhance clinical applicability and potentially improve efficacy. However, the clinical effectiveness of this approach remains unclear.

pmc-11430293.title: Rotenone-Induced Optic Nerve Damage and Retinal Ganglion Cell Loss in Rats
pmc-11430293.creator: Yasuko Yamamoto, Takazumi Taniguchi, Atsushi Shimazaki
pmc-11430293.description: Rotenone is a mitochondrial complex I inhibitor that causes retinal degeneration. A study of a rat model of rotenone-induced retinal degeneration suggested that this model is caused by indirect postsynaptic N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) stimulation triggered by oxidative stress-mediated presynaptic intracellular calcium signaling.

pmc-11455937.title: 3D bioprinting of fish skin-based gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA) bio-ink for use as a potential skin substitute
pmc-11455937.creator: Nuttapol Tanadchangsaeng, Kitipong Pasanaphong, Tulyapruek Tawonsawatruk, Kasem Rattanapinyopituk, Borwornporn Tangketsarawan, Visut Rawiwet, Alita Kongchanagul, Narongrit Srikaew, Thanaporn Yoyruerop, Nattapon Panupinthu, Ratirat Sangpayap, Anuchan Panaksri, Sani Boonyagul, Ruedee Hemstapat
pmc-11455937.description: Gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA), typically derived from mammalian sources, has recently emerged as an ideal bio-ink for three-dimensional (3D) bioprinting. Herein, we developed a fish skin-based GelMA bio-ink for the fabrication of a 3D GelMA skin substitute with a 3D bioprinter. Several concentrations of methacrylic acid anhydride were used to fabricate GelMA, in which their physical-mechanical properties were assessed.

pmc-11590924.title: Effects of a Gastroscopic Procedure on Salivary Cortisol Release and Fecal Cortisol Metabolites in Young Racehorses
pmc-11590924.creator: Sabina Ostermeier, Rupert Palme, Ingrid Vervuert, Barbara Glomm, Karsten Feige, Sabine Macho-Maschler, Uta König von Borstel, Monica Venner, Amir Steinman
pmc-11590924.description: Simple SummaryGastroscopy is a minimally invasive, safe method to evaluate the equine stomach. This procedure is important for a precise diagnosis in case of suspected gastric disease for the adequate treatment and management of equine patients. However, horses might experience stress while undergoing gastroscopy.

pmc-12605744.title: The political economy of adolescent mental health in Kenya
pmc-12605744.creator: Albert Tele, Darius Nyamai, Yusra Ribhi Shawar, Vincent Nyongesa, Samuel Kiogora, Stefan Swartling Peterson, Georgina Obonyo, Pim Cuijpers, Manasi Kumar
pmc-12605744.description: Adolescent mental health remains a critical yet under-prioritized issue in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) like Kenya, where resource limitations, stigma, and systemic barriers hinder access to care. While policies and strategies such as Kenya's Mental Health Action Plan (2021–2025) exist on paper, their implementation is constrained by limited resources and a weak mental health service delivery infrastructure.

pmc-12615604.title: Optimization of selective catalytic reduction for nox emission control: an experimental and CFD analysis of mixer designs
pmc-12615604.creator: Swetha Bandaru, Jayaprabakar Jayaraman, K. Vijetha, Ashish Kumar, G. Hariharan, Man Mohan, Abhishek Sharma, Hemant Raj Singh
pmc-12615604.description: This study focuses on optimizing the selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system to reduce urea deposits and enhance overall system performance. Both computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations and experimental analyses were conducted to evaluate an S-bend inlet SCR design and an improved configuration featuring multiple mixer setups.

pmc-12966935.title: NCOA2 promotes the return of hematopoietic stem cells to quiescence after irradiation stress by regulating FOXO3a‐dependent mitophagy
pmc-12966935.creator: Fang Chen, Naicheng Chen, Linjie Wang, Hao Zeng, Yukai Lu, Yanying Liu, Jing Chen, Yang Xu, Mo Chen, Song Wang, Mingqiang Shen, Junping Wang, Mengjia Hu
pmc-12966935.description: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) are responsible for replenishing blood cells under stress conditions through increasing proliferation and differentiation. After the hematopoietic function has reconstructed, HSCs must re‐enter a quiescent state to avoid their depletion, whereas the underlying mechanisms remain to be elucidated.

pmc-13109317.title: Design of a binocular multispectral stereo imaging system and its application in plant phenotyping
pmc-13109317.creator: Wenxiu Wan, Zhiyuan Liu, Ziru Yu, Jiahui Wang, Xiangyang Yu
pmc-13109317.description: With the continuous progress in micro-optical machine technology, miniature spectral imaging devices have been rapidly developed; however, three-dimensional (3D) imaging measurement technology has become increasingly mature and widely used. The evolution of these technologies has established a robust foundation for the integration of three-dimensional imaging and spectral information.

pmc-13146976.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1045 TEMPORAL DYNAMICS OF DWI LESION VOLUME IN ACUTE STROKE AND ITS CLINICAL RELEVANCE
pmc-13146976.creator: Nakhoon Kim, Hyeran Kim, Jinyoung Kim, Keun-Sik Hong, Mark Parsons, Umberto Pensato, Johanna Ospel, Wi Sun Ryu, Jihoon Kang, Moon-Ku Han, Hee-Joon Bae, Beom Joon Kim
pmc-13146976.description: Background and aimsWhile infarcts are known to expand after stroke onset, the clinical relevance of quantitative DWI lesion volume dynamics in a large ischemic stroke cohort remains under-investigated.MethodsWe analyzed 8,576 consecutive patients from a prospective registry with paired DWI scans (baseline <24h; follow-up 24–168h). Lesion volumes were automatically quantified.

pmc-13268883.title: Immunomodulation by platelet-derived DKK1: potential for controlling disease and pathology in leishmaniasis and implications for other infectious diseases
pmc-13268883.creator: Olivia C. Ihedioha, Diane McMahon-Pratt, Alfred L. M. Bothwell
pmc-13268883.description: Parasitic infection caused by Leishmania major in BALB/c mice is a well-established example of a chronic inflammatory disease. Although chronic inflammation in parasitic infections stems from persistent interactions between parasites and host immune cells, the mechanisms by which parasitic infections induce and regulate chronic immune responses remain to be fully understood.
